text: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men out from Shittim as spies, saying, "Go, look over the land, especially Jericho." So they went and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed there.
The king of Jericho was told, "Look, men have come here tonight from the Israelites to search out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they have come to search out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
At dark, when it was time to shut the gate, the men left. I don't know where they went. Go after them quickly—you may overtake them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out there.
So the pursuers went after them along the road toward the Jordan, as far as the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as they had gone out.

versions.text: So the men pursued them along the road toward the Jordan, to the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out.
versions.explanation: "The men" in verses 4-5 refers to the spies, so repeating "the men" here is momentarily confusing for a listener. Naming them as the pursuers at the start (and using a pronoun at the end) clarifies who is chasing whom without adding content.

text: Before the spies lay down for the night, she came up to them on the roof
and said to them, "I know that the LORD has given you this land, that dread of you has fallen upon us, and that all who live in this land are melting away before you.

For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you utterly destroyed.
When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no courage was left in anyone because of you; for the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
Now then, swear to me by the LORD that, since I have shown you kindness, you will also show kindness to my father's house. Give me a sure sign
that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and deliver us from death."
The men said to her, "Our lives for yours! If you do not report this business of ours, then when the LORD gives us the land we will deal kindly and faithfully with you."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, and she lived in the wall itself.
She said to them, "Go into the hill country, so the pursuers will not come upon you. Hide there three days until they return; after that you can go on your way."

versions.text: She said to them, "Head for the hills, so the pursuers will not find you. Hide there three days until they return; after that you can go on your way."
versions.explanation: "Head for the hills" is a colloquial English idiom with humorous/flippant overtones that clashes with the tone of the narrative. "Hill country" better renders הָהָר (the mountainous region west of Jericho), and "come upon" is closer to יִפְגְּעוּ בָכֶם (encounter/meet) than "find."

text: The men said to her, "We will be released from this oath you have made us swear

unless, when we enter the land, you tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and gather your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's household into your house.

If anyone goes out the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be innocent. But if a hand is laid on anyone who is with you in the house, his blood will be on our heads.
And if you report this business of ours, we will be released from the oath you made us swear."
"Let it be as you say," she replied. She sent them away, and they departed; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They left and went into the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers had searched all along the road but did not find them.

versions.text: They left and went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers had searched all along the road and found nothing.
versions.explanation: The object of לֹא מָצָאוּ is the spies, not "nothing" in general; "did not find them" is more accurate and keeps the narrative focus on the men. Also aligns the wording of "hill country" with verse 16.

text: Then the two men started back. They came down from the hills, crossed over, and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land into our hands; all who live in the land are melting away before us."
